name: Dubai Islamic Bank
founded: 1975 (incorporated by Amiri Decree of the Ruler of Dubai on 12 March 1975; later registered as a public joint stock company). Absorbed Noor Bank (100% owned; operations integrated from November 2020).
ownership_summary: Listed on DFM. The only shareholder above 5% is Investment Corporation of Dubai (ICD), with 2,024,955,636 shares or 27.97% at 31 Dec 2025 (shareholder table; the related-party note rounds it to 27.9%). ICD is majority-owned by the Government of Dubai.

shareholders.holder: Investment Corporation of Dubai (majority-owned by the Government of Dubai)

government_link: Yes. Investment Corporation of Dubai (majority-owned by the Government of Dubai) holds 27.97% (31 Dec 2025). The former chairman (to 20 Sep 2026) was Director-General of the Dubai Ruler's Court and Managing Director of ICD.
group_structure: Parent bank in the UAE (CBUAE-licensed; SCA introducer licence for brokerage referrals). Material subsidiaries at 30 Jun 2026: Dubai Islamic Bank Pakistan (100%), Noor Bank (100%, integrated), Tamweel PSC (92%, financing), DIB Bank Kenya (100%), Deyaar Development PJSC (44.9%, consolidated real-estate developer), Dar Al Sharia Islamic Finance Consultancy (100%, Shariah advisory), plus property, services and SPV entities. Dubai Islamic Financial Services LLC, the brokerage subsidiary (100% at 31 Dec 2025), was liquidated during H1 2026. Equity-accounted associates and JVs at 31 Dec 2025 include Bank of Khartoum (29.5%), PT Bank Panin Dubai Syariah Tbk (25.1%), Bosnia Bank International (27.3%), Liquidity Management Center Bahrain (25%) and the T.O.M. group in Türkiye (25%; digital bank 'HADI' app). No separate group files exist in this database, so all figures here are group consolidated.

subsidiaries.activity: Digital participation bank and payments/finance companies, Türkiye (equity-accounted; up from 20% in 2024)

footprint: UAE: 56 branches and 530+ ATMs/CDMs (AR 2025). Banking subsidiaries in Pakistan and Kenya; associates in Indonesia, Bosnia, Sudan, Türkiye and Bahrain. The bank says it operates in seven countries across three continents and reaches more than 5 million customers (AR 2025).
customer_segments: Retail (Consumer Banking incl. Emirati Banking and Johara Ladies Banking), affluent tiers Mumayyaz Privilege Banking and Aayan Exclusive Banking, Wajaha Private Banking, business banking/SME and emerging corporates (Commercial Banking), corporate and institutional, sovereign and GRE clients (Investment Banking, Treasury).
business_lines: Consumer Banking (retail deposits, personal, home and auto finance, cards, 'priority banking and wealth management' per segment note); Corporate Banking; Commercial Banking (SME and emerging corporates, created 2022 onward); Investment Banking (debt capital markets, where DIB says it ranked 3rd globally among sukuk bookrunners in 2024 and 2025, an equity capital markets franchise using corporate and private banking channels for IPO distribution, and structured and cross-border finance); Treasury (sukuk book, FX, client sukuk and structured-product sales); international subsidiaries and real estate. Wealth products (third-party Shariah funds and ETFs, sukuk, structured products, managed portfolios) are sold through relationship managers in the Mumayyaz, Aayan and Wajaha tiers. Brokerage is referred to Al Ramz Capital.

capabilities.wealth_summary: DIB runs wealth through Consumer Banking (under the Chief Consumer Banking Officer) in three published tiers: Mumayyaz Privilege Banking (AED 100k–350k relationship), Aayan Exclusive Banking (AED 750k) and Wajaha Private Banking (AED 3.5m), each with relationship managers and dedicated centres. The shelf is relationship-manager-led and fully Shariah-compliant: a 19-line list of third-party Shariah funds and ETFs (HSBC, iShares, Franklin Templeton, Aditum, Azimut, Old Mutual, Oasis Crescent, ASB/State Street, mostly 'Professional' category, dated 12 Oct 2026), sukuk via a dedicated trading desk, structured products, REITs, share finance and FX. Mumayyaz advertises managed portfolios in conservative, balanced and aggressive options, with fund-manager selection by Morningstar Investment Management Europe. Equity brokerage is referred to Al Ramz Capital under DIB's SCA introducer licence (alliance dated 17 Nov 2022), and the in-house brokerage subsidiary Dubai Islamic Financial Services was liquidated in H1 2026. The DIB alt app (1.1m registered users) lists only 'open investment deposit account' as an investment service. No AUM or wealth client assets are disclosed; fiduciary assets were AED 11.7bn at end 2025.

segments.name: Mumayyaz Privilege Banking
segments.eligibility: Relationship of AED 100,000–350,000 or monthly salary credit of AED 15,000–35,000 (as published); Mumayyaz desks in 40+ branches, 90+ relationship officers

segments.name: Aayan Exclusive Banking
segments.eligibility: Account balance of AED 750,000 or more, or salary credit of AED 50,000 (UAE nationals) / AED 60,000 (expatriates); monthly fee if not met; Aayan centres across the UAE

segments.name: Wajaha Private Banking
segments.eligibility: Relationship of AED 3,500,000 or salary credit of AED 150,000; otherwise AED 200 monthly membership fee; Wajaha centres in Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah and Al Ain

private_banking.detail: Wajaha Private Banking (AED 3.5m threshold): dedicated relationship manager, Wajaha centres in four cities, Wakala deposits, structured products, commodities, mutual funds, REITs and share finance. Wajaha clients made up more than 60% of client sukuk sales volumes in 2025 (AR). No head of private banking is named on official pages.

asset_management.detail: No asset-management subsidiary in the H1 2026 subsidiary list (FS note 28) and no DIB-branded funds on the fund list, which is entirely third-party. DIB FM Ltd (Cayman) is listed only as an investment SPV.

brokerage.detail: Referral model: 'Trading Services' via Al Ramz Capital LLC under DIB's SCA introducer licence (alliance announced 17 Nov 2022). Covers ADX, DFM, Nasdaq Dubai and Saudi markets, plus Oman, Bahrain and Astana via the ADX Tabadul hub, on an unnamed Al Ramz online platform with an 'Islamic trading mode' and 10-minute online onboarding. The in-house broker Dubai Islamic Financial Services LLC was liquidated in H1 2026, though the Wajaha and Aayan pages still mention it.

digital_investing.detail: No in-app investing in securities or funds found. The DIB alt app (launched as an umbrella brand on 4 Jun 2023, 135+ services) lists only 'Open investment deposit account' among its services. Online equity trading needs a separate Al Ramz Capital account and platform (see brokerage).

advisory.detail: Relationship managers and 'Investment Specialists' present the product suite to wealth customers. Wajaha RMs 'personally analyse your portfolio and offer the best advice'. Aayan offers professional advice at Aayan centres.

discretionary.detail: Mumayyaz advertises 'managed portfolios' with risk-based allocation and a flexible fee structure, but the page does not say whether they are discretionary mandates or advisory model portfolios.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: Mumayyaz managed portfolios in conservative, balanced and aggressive versions, diversified across Shariah-compliant equity and fixed income, with fund-manager selection by Morningstar Investment Management Europe. Aayan lists 'mutual fund-based portfolios'. These are relationship-manager-distributed; no robo or digital model-portfolio service found.

funds_platform.detail: Mutual Fund List 'as on 12-Oct-2026': 19 third-party Shariah lines, comprising 4 sukuk funds, 5 global equity funds, 7 Islamic UCITS ETFs and 3 multi-asset funds, from HSBC (6), iShares/BlackRock (3), Franklin Templeton (3), Aditum (2), Azimut (2), Old Mutual, Oasis Crescent and ASB/State Street. 15 of 19 are 'Professional' category. Separate fund charge schedules exist for Aayan and Wajaha customers. Platform provider not named.

structured_products.detail: Structured products listed for Wajaha. Aayan lists Islamic portfolios covering structured products and currency- and commodity-linked structures. Treasury reports digitisation of client experience across sukuk, FX and structured products and new ESG-aligned Shariah investment products in 2025.

private_markets.detail: No private equity, private credit or alternatives offering found on wealth or investment-product pages, the fund list or AR 2025. REITs are listed for Wajaha.

islamic_wealth.detail: Fully Shariah-compliant bank under its Internal Sharia Supervision Committee and the CBUAE Higher Sharia Authority. All funds, ETFs, sukuk and portfolios on the shelf are Shariah products. DIB's Group Head of Internal Sharia Audit is Vice Chairman of the Unified Sharia Screening Committee for DFM/ADX securities.

AR 2025 states an aspiration to deepen digital and product platforms 'from wealth tech, digital banking, and embedded finance to impact investing and Islamic fintech'. 5-year strategy (2022–26) includes 'launch of a new digital proposition' and 'build ancillary business and newer revenue streams'
Dubai Islamic Financial Services LLC (brokerage subsidiary) liquidated during H1 2026

opportunities: No digital investing: the DIB alt app (1.1m registered users, 55% of transactions in H1 2026) offers only investment deposits, and equities need a separate Al Ramz account (S4, S14, S17).
Wealth shelf is RM-led and mostly 'Professional'-category: 15 of 19 listed funds/ETFs are professional-only, and no private-markets products were found (S15).
Brokerage subsidiary DIFS was liquidated in H1 2026, so execution and investment services now rely on partners (S3, S14).
AR 2025 names 'wealth tech' among platforms to deepen; the 2022–26 strategy cycle ends in 2026, and DIB just added Finshape and HCLTech as digital/AI partners (S5, S20).
Large affluent and private base by tier (Mumayyaz, Aayan, Wajaha) with published thresholds; Wajaha clients drove more than 60% of client sukuk sales in 2025 (S5, S10–S12).
barriers: Fully Islamic: every product needs Internal Sharia Supervision Committee approval and CBUAE Higher Sharia Authority alignment (S3, S5).

Existing partners cover parts of the wealth stack: Al Ramz Capital (brokerage), Morningstar Investment Management (portfolio fund selection), Finshape DBOS (digital channels) and an IBM/HCLTech data and AI relationship (S5, S12, S14, S19, S20).
Leadership change at board level: new Chairman from 30 Sep 2026 and board composition changed since AR 2025; strategy priorities for the next cycle not yet published (S2, S7).
Results emphasise financing, sukuk/DCM and deposits. No wealth AUM, fee or client metrics are disclosed, so wealth may be a low reported priority (S4, S6).
